【原视频简介】
Can FreeToken make huge local AI models fast when they do not fit inside your GPU?

FreeToken is a new open-source local inference engine designed for one difficult problem: running large Mixture-of-Experts models across GPU VRAM and system RAM without wasting the GPU on constant weight transfers.

In the FreeToken paper, an RTX 4060 laptop with only 8GB of VRAM ran Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B at 39.3 tokens per second. On an RTX 5090, DeepSeek V4 Flash reached more than 20 tokens per second — despite being far too large to fit entirely in GPU memory.

This video compares FreeToken vs llama.cpp and explains what those results actually mean for local AI, coding agents, large-context workflows and MoE inference.

FreeToken is not a new model. It is the runtime that decides which model experts stay in VRAM, which remain in system RAM, when to transfer them across PCIe, and when the CPU may be faster than waiting for the GPU.
